docs.title: TraceAPI
docs.text: TraceAPI is a FastAPI service for 3D neuron tracing. It wraps bundled neuTube and Vaa3D APP2/smartTrace binaries, accepts uploaded TIFF volumes or server-side TIFF paths, and returns SWC reconstructions.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• neuTube tracing for uploaded or server-side volumes.
  • Vaa3D APP2 and smartTrace tracing.
  • Directional subtree extraction from ordered seed pairs s1 -> s2.
  • Batch seed-pair support: one SWC for a single pair, ZIP for multiple pairs.
  • Temporary run outputs under runs/, cleaned periodically by the service.

docs.title: Repository Layout
docs.text:
app.py             FastAPI routes
app_helpers.py     upload, workdir, subprocess, and volume-prep helpers
subtree_utils.py   seed parsing and swclib-based subtree extraction
vaa3d_utils.py     Vaa3D/SWC utility functions
algorithms/        bundled neuTube, Vaa3D, Qt libraries, and plugins
docs/              MkDocs documentation source
mkdocs.yml         MkDocs Material configuration

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Python 3.9+
  • Vaa3D/Qt system libraries
  • Python packages: fastapi, uvicorn, python-multipart, numpy, scipy, tifffile, swclib

Install common system dependencies:

sudo apt-get install -y xvfb libglu1-mesa \
  libqt5widgets5 libqt5gui5 libqt5xml5 libqt5network5 libqt5core5a libqt5concurrent5

Install Python dependencies:

pip install fastapi uvicorn python-multipart numpy scipy tifffile
pip install -e /path/to/swclib

docs.title: Run Locally
docs.text:
Xvfb :99 -screen 0 1920x1080x24 -ac &
export DISPLAY=:99
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH="$PWD/algorithms:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH"
python -m uvicorn app:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 --workers 4

docs.title: Quick Example
docs.text:
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/trace_vaa3d_app2_subtree \
  -F "tif_path=/data2/public_data/CWMBS/image/SN21.tif" \
  -F "s1=242.8440,249.8640,7.9980" \
  -F "s2=243.5728,248.0015,7.9980" \
  --output SN21_seed1_app2.swc

docs.title: Algorithms
docs.text: This page describes what happens inside each tracing route: image preprocessing, the iterative tracing loops, and directional subtree extraction. The behavior described here comes from app.py, vaa3d_utils.py, and subtree_utils.py.

docs.title: Coordinate Conventions
docs.text:
Images are read as (Z, Y, X) (D, H, W) arrays. Seed points are given as x, y, z.

Vaa3D writes SWC coordinates with a flipped Y axis relative to the input stack. After every Vaa3D trace, postprocess_vaa3d_result rewrites each node's y to H - 1 - y and forces the node type to 0, bringing the SWC back into the image coordinate frame. neuTube output is not flipped.

Markers handed to Vaa3D APP2 are written with the same flip (write_marker_file): x+1, H - y, z+1, each clamped into the volume bounds.

docs.title: Preprocessing
docs.text:
Every route normalizes the input the same way before tracing:

  1. Read the volume with tifffile.
  2. Min-max scale to uint8 [0, 255] (to_uint8_0_255).
  3. Require a 3D array.
  4. Write vol_uint8.tiff into the run directory as the tracer input.

docs.title: neuTube (/trace_neutube, /trace_neutube_subtree)
docs.text:
neuTube is invoked once per request:

neuTube --command <input> --trace -o <output.swc> --level 0

There is no iterative masking loop for neuTube. The traced SWC is returned directly (plain route) or fed into subtree extraction (subtree route).

docs.title: Vaa3D APP2 — full volume (/trace_vaa3d_app2)
docs.text:
APP2 is run iteratively to recover multiple neurites (run_trace_iterative_with_seed_fallback):

  • Settings: max_iters=32, timeout_sec=3000, min_nodes_to_accept=3, max_seed_tries_per_iter=8.
  • Each iteration runs APP2 on the current (progressively masked) volume.
  • Auto mode: APP2 runs with no marker. If it yields nodes, they are kept.
  • Seed-fallback mode: if auto tracing yields zero nodes while meaningful foreground remains (>20 non-zero voxels), the loop switches to seeded tracing. A candidate seed pool is built from distance-transform / intensity local maxima (build_neutube_like_seed_pool), and up to max_seed_tries_per_iter seeds are tried per iteration until one produces a trace.
  • Acceptance: an iteration's SWC is kept only if it has at least min_nodes_to_accept nodes and total length >= 3.0.
  • Masking: the traced tree is rasterized to a sphere/cone mask (swc_to_mask_sphere_cone, r_scale=3.0) and erased from the volume so the next iteration finds different structure. Covered candidate seeds are dropped.
  • The loop ends when an iteration produces no nodes, max_iters is reached, or the time budget expires.

All accepted SWCs are merged (merge_swcs) into output.swc. If nothing was accepted, the route returns 422.

docs.title: APP2 parameters
docs.text:
The APP2 plugin is called as:

Vaa3D-x -x vn2 -f app2 -i <vol_uint8.tiff> -o <out.swc> -p \
  <marker|None> 0 10 0 1 0 0 5 1 0 0
Position Value Meaning 1 <marker> / None input marker file 2 0 channel 3 10 background threshold 4 0 b_256cube 5 1 b_radiusFrom2D 6 0 is_gsdt 7 0 is_gap 8 5 length threshold 9 1 is_resample 10 0 is_brightfield 11 0 is_high_intensity

docs.title: Vaa3D APP2 — subtree (/trace_vaa3d_app2_subtree)
docs.text:
This route does not use the iterative loop. For each seed pair it:

  1. Writes a marker file at s1.
  2. Runs APP2 once from that marker (timeout_sec=600).
  3. Extracts the directional subtree (see below).

If APP2 fails for any pair the request returns 422 APP2 failed for seed pair <i>.

docs.title: Vaa3D smartTrace (/trace_vaa3d_smartTrace)
docs.text:
smartTrace runs iteratively with a denoise fallback (run_trace_iterative_with_noise_mask):

  • Settings: max_iters=16, timeout_sec=3000, min_nodes_to_accept=3.
  • Each iteration runs smartTrace, which writes <input>_smartTracing.swc; that file is renamed to the iteration output.
  • Denoise fallback: if an iteration yields zero nodes while foreground remains (>10 non-zero voxels), tiny/compact connected components are removed once (denoise_foreground_components_inplace) and the iteration retries.
  • Acceptance / masking: same node-count and length rules and the same sphere/cone masking as APP2.
  • Unlike APP2, if nothing is accepted this route still returns a (possibly empty) merged output.swc rather than raising 422.

docs.title: Directional Subtree Extraction
docs.text:
For each ordered pair s1 -> s2, filter_one_swc_subtree turns a full reconstruction into the single branch leaving s1 toward s2:

  1. Compute sample_distance = ||s1 - s2||; reject if zero.
  2. Find the SWC node nearest s1. If none exists, return a canonical empty (0-node) SWC for this pair instead of failing.
  3. Reroot the tree at that node (get_rerooted_tree).
  4. Resample the rerooted tree with spacing equal to sample_distance (resample), saved without header and reindexed.
  5. Among the root's children, keep only the child branch whose direction best aligns with the target direction — the smallest angle (angle_between_vectors) between the child's root -> child vector and the root -> s2 vector. Detach the other branches.
  6. Save the resulting subtree.

The target direction is measured from the branch point (the resampled root, the node nearest s1), not from s1 itself, so both vectors share an origin. Degenerate (zero-length) child vectors and any NaN angle from floating-point error are treated as the worst case and never selected.

A single pair yields subtree.swc; multiple pairs are zipped into subtrees.zip (zip_swc_files), which rejects any missing or empty member with 500.

docs.title: Run Directories & Cleanup
docs.text: Each request gets a timestamped working directory under runs/ (make_workdir) holding the normalized volume, intermediate SWCs, markers, and log.txt. A background thread (cleanup_runs_worker) started at app startup deletes run directories older than 1 hour, checking every 30 minutes.

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text:
Base URL for local service examples:

http://127.0.0.1:8000

The GitHub Pages URL is documentation-only — the live service runs wherever you deploy it:

https://yang-ze-kang.github.io/TraceAPI/

docs.title: Endpoint Summary
docs.text:
Method & Path Input Success response POST /trace_neutube file output.swc POST /trace_neutube_subtree file or tif_path, s1, s2 subtree.swc or subtrees.zip POST /trace_vaa3d_app2 file output.swc POST /trace_vaa3d_app2_subtree file or tif_path, s1, s2 subtree.swc or subtrees.zip POST /trace_vaa3d_smartTrace file output.swc

All requests are multipart/form-data. All successful tracing responses are SWC files (application/octet-stream); multi-pair subtree responses are ZIP archives (application/zip).

See Input Formats for seed/volume rules and Errors for status codes. For request/response snippets in curl and Python, see Client Examples.

docs.title: POST /trace_neutube
docs.text:
Run neuTube tracing on an uploaded volume and return the full reconstruction.

Name Required Type Description file yes file 3D input volume (multipart upload).

Returns: output.swc.

curlPython 
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/trace_neutube \
  -F "file=@/path/to/volume.tif" \
  --output output.swc

from pathlib import Path
import requests

url = "http://127.0.0.1:8000/trace_neutube"
with open("/path/to/volume.tif", "rb") as f:
    resp = requests.post(url, files={"file": f}, timeout=None)
resp.raise_for_status()
Path("output.swc").write_bytes(resp.content)

docs.title: POST /trace_neutube_subtree
docs.text:
Run neuTube tracing, then extract directional subtrees from one or more seed pairs.

Name Required Type Description file one of file/tif_path file Uploaded input volume. tif_path one of file/tif_path string Server-side input path. s1 yes string Start seed point(s). s2 yes string Direction seed point(s).

Returns: subtree.swc for one pair, or subtrees.zip for multiple pairs.

curlPython 
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/trace_neutube_subtree \
  -F "tif_path=/data2/public_data/CWMBS/image/SN21.tif" \
  -F "s1=242.8440,249.8640,7.9980" \
  -F "s2=243.5728,248.0015,7.9980" \
  --output SN21_seed1_neuTube.swc

from pathlib import Path
import requests

url = "http://127.0.0.1:8000/trace_neutube_subtree"
data = {
    "tif_path": "/data2/public_data/CWMBS/image/SN21.tif",
    "s1": "242.8440,249.8640,7.9980",
    "s2": "243.5728,248.0015,7.9980",
}
resp = requests.post(url, data=data, timeout=None)
resp.raise_for_status()
Path("SN21_seed1_neuTube.swc").write_bytes(resp.content)

docs.title: POST /trace_vaa3d_app2
docs.text:
Run iterative Vaa3D APP2 tracing on an uploaded volume. The service repeatedly traces, accepts and masks out each branch, and falls back to candidate seeds when automatic tracing finds nothing. See Algorithms.

Name Required Type Description file yes file 3D input volume (multipart upload).

Returns: merged output.swc. Returns 422 if no branch is accepted.

curlPython 
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/trace_vaa3d_app2 \
  -F "file=@/path/to/volume.tif" \
  --output app2.swc

from pathlib import Path
import requests

url = "http://127.0.0.1:8000/trace_vaa3d_app2"
with open("/path/to/volume.tif", "rb") as f:
    resp = requests.post(url, files={"file": f}, timeout=None)
resp.raise_for_status()
Path("app2.swc").write_bytes(resp.content)

docs.title: POST /trace_vaa3d_app2_subtree
docs.text:
Run Vaa3D APP2 from each s1 marker, then apply the same directional extraction used by neuTube subtree tracing. Unlike the full APP2 route, this runs APP2 once per seed pair (no iterative masking loop).

Name Required Type Description file one of file/tif_path file Uploaded input volume. tif_path one of file/tif_path string Server-side input path. s1 yes string APP2 marker/start seed point(s). s2 yes string Direction seed point(s).

Returns: subtree.swc for one pair, or subtrees.zip for multiple pairs. Returns 422 APP2 failed for seed pair <i> if tracing fails for any pair.

  -F "s1=242.8440,249.8640,7.9980" \
  -F "s2=243.5728,248.0015,7.9980" \

docs.title: POST /trace_vaa3d_smartTrace

Run iterative Vaa3D smartTrace tracing on an uploaded volume, with a one-time foreground denoise fallback when a pass finds nothing. See Algorithms.

Name Required Type Description file yes file 3D input volume (multipart upload).

Returns: merged output.swc. May return an empty merge if nothing is traced; an empty/zero-byte result then triggers 500.

curlPython

  -F "file=@/path/to/volume.tif" \
  --output smarttrace.swc

with open("/path/to/volume.tif", "rb") as f:
    resp = requests.post(url, files={"file": f}, timeout=None)
resp.raise_for_status()
Path("smarttrace.swc").write_bytes(resp.content)

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• The GitHub Pages site is static documentation only.
  • The FastAPI service must run on a server with access to the tracing binaries and input data.
  • tif_path values are resolved on the API server, not in the browser.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
All errors are returned as standard FastAPI/Starlette JSON with a detail field:

{ "detail": "Provide exactly one of file or tif_path" }

The tables below list every error the service raises, grouped by status code, with the condition that triggers it.

docs.title: 400 — Bad Request
docs.text:
Client input problems. The request never reaches the tracer.

detail Condition Unsupported file type: <suffix> File suffix not in the allowed set. Provide exactly one of file or tif_path Subtree route received both or neither input. tif_path not found: <path> tif_path does not exist or is not a regular file. Expected 3D volume, got shape=<shape> Image read as a non-3D array. <name> cannot be empty s1/s2 was an empty string. <name> must contain exactly 3 numbers A seed point did not have 3 components. <name> contains non-numeric values A seed component failed to parse as a float. <name>[<i>] must contain 3 numbers A JSON seed item was not a 3-number array. At least one seed pair is required No seed points were parsed. s1 and s2 must contain the same number of points Mismatched seed counts. s1 and s2 must be different points A pair had zero distance between s1 and s2.

docs.title: 422 — Unprocessable Entity
docs.text:
The tracer ran, but no usable reconstruction could be produced.

detail Condition <label> failed for auto and candidate seeds. APP2 iterative tracing produced no accepted SWC (auto + seed fallback). APP2 failed for seed pair <i> APP2 subtree route could not trace from a given s1 marker. Resampled SWC has no root Resampling collapsed the tree to nothing. Resampled SWC has no valid target node No node near s2 after resampling.

No node near s1

When subtree extraction finds no traced node near s1, it does not raise 422. It returns a canonical empty (0-node) SWC so a single bad seed never fails a batch. The file is a valid SWC that parses to zero nodes — check the node count to detect this case.

smartTrace failure mode

/trace_vaa3d_smartTrace does not raise 422 when nothing is traced. It merges whatever SWCs were accepted (possibly an empty SWC) and returns the file. If the result is empty, the final 500 output.swc not generated or empty check applies instead.

docs.title: 500 — Internal Server Error
docs.text:
Server/environment problems or a failed external command.

detail Condition <name> not found: <path> A tracer binary is missing. <name> not executable: <path> A tracer binary lacks the execute bit. Failed to save upload: <error> Writing the uploaded file failed. Command failed. Tail log:\n<...> A tracer exited with a non-zero status; the last ~5000 chars of the run log are included. output.swc not generated or empty The expected output file is missing or zero bytes. subtree.swc not generated or empty A subtree output is missing or zero bytes. <name> not generated or empty A file destined for the ZIP was missing or empty.

docs.title: Timeouts
docs.text: Each tracer invocation runs under a timeout. The iterative loops also enforce a total time budget (timeout_sec). When a tracing iteration exceeds its budget the loop stops early and returns whatever has been accepted so far rather than erroring — see Algorithms. A single command that exceeds its own subprocess timeout is killed; the loop treats that iteration as producing no output.

docs.title: Client Examples
docs.text:
End-to-end examples for calling TraceAPI from the command line and from Python. The Python examples use requests:

pip install requests

In every example, replace http://127.0.0.1:8000 with your server address and adjust paths to your data.

docs.title: Uploading a Local File
docs.text:
Send a volume from the client machine as a multipart upload.

curlPython 
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/trace_neutube \
  -F "file=@/path/to/volume.tif" \
  --output output.swc

from pathlib import Path
import requests

url = "http://127.0.0.1:8000/trace_neutube"
with open("/path/to/volume.tif", "rb") as f:
    resp = requests.post(url, files={"file": f}, timeout=None)
resp.raise_for_status()
Path("output.swc").write_bytes(resp.content)
print("saved output.swc")

Use timeout=None

Tracing can take minutes. Pass timeout=None (or a generous timeout) so the client does not abort a long-running trace.

docs.title: Referencing a Server-Side Path
docs.text:
Subtree routes accept tif_path, a path resolved on the server. No file is uploaded — only the path string is sent as a form field.

curlPython 
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/trace_vaa3d_app2_subtree \
  -F "tif_path=/data2/public_data/CWMBS/image/SN21.tif" \
  -F "s1=242.8440,249.8640,7.9980" \
  -F "s2=243.5728,248.0015,7.9980" \
  --output SN21_seed1_app2.swc

from pathlib import Path
import requests

url = "http://127.0.0.1:8000/trace_vaa3d_app2_subtree"
data = {
    "tif_path": "/data2/public_data/CWMBS/image/SN21.tif",
    "s1": "242.8440,249.8640,7.9980",
    "s2": "243.5728,248.0015,7.9980",
}
resp = requests.post(url, data=data, timeout=None)
resp.raise_for_status()
Path("SN21_seed1_app2.swc").write_bytes(resp.content)

docs.title: Batch Seed Pairs (ZIP Response)
docs.text:
When you send more than one seed pair, the response is a ZIP containing one SWC per pair. Detect it via the Content-Type header.

curlPython 
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/trace_neutube_subtree \
  -F "tif_path=/path/to/volume.tif" \
  -F "s1=10,20,30;40,50,60" \
  -F "s2=11,20,30;42,50,60" \
  --output subtrees.zip

import io
import zipfile
from pathlib import Path
import requests

url = "http://127.0.0.1:8000/trace_neutube_subtree"
data = {
    "tif_path": "/path/to/volume.tif",
    "s1": "10,20,30;40,50,60",
    "s2": "11,20,30;42,50,60",
}
resp = requests.post(url, data=data, timeout=None)
resp.raise_for_status()

content_type = resp.headers.get("content-type", "")
if "zip" in content_type:
    with zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(resp.content)) as zf:
        zf.extractall("subtrees")
    print("extracted", zf.namelist())
else:
    Path("subtree.swc").write_bytes(resp.content)

docs.title: JSON Seed Arrays
docs.text:
s1/s2 also accept JSON arrays (see Input Formats).

import json
import requests

url = "http://127.0.0.1:8000/trace_vaa3d_app2_subtree"
data = {
    "tif_path": "/path/to/volume.tif",
    "s1": json.dumps([[10, 20, 30], [40, 50, 60]]),
    "s2": json.dumps([[11, 20, 30], [42, 50, 60]]),
}
resp = requests.post(url, data=data, timeout=None)
resp.raise_for_status()

docs.title: Handling Errors
docs.text:
Errors come back as JSON with a detail field (see Errors).

import requests

url = "http://127.0.0.1:8000/trace_vaa3d_app2"
with open("/path/to/volume.tif", "rb") as f:
    resp = requests.post(url, files={"file": f}, timeout=None)

if not resp.ok:
    try:
        detail = resp.json().get("detail")
    except ValueError:
        detail = resp.text
    raise SystemExit(f"Tracing failed ({resp.status_code}): {detail}")

with open("app2.swc", "wb") as out:
    out.write(resp.content)

docs.title: A Reusable Client
docs.text:
A small wrapper that auto-saves .swc or .zip based on the response type:

from pathlib import Path
import requests


class TraceClient:
    def __init__(self, base_url="http://127.0.0.1:8000"):
        self.base_url = base_url.rstrip("/")

    def _post(self, route, *, files=None, data=None):
        resp = requests.post(
            f"{self.base_url}{route}", files=files, data=data, timeout=None
        )
        if not resp.ok:
            try:
                detail = resp.json().get("detail")
            except ValueError:
                detail = resp.text
            raise RuntimeError(f"{resp.status_code}: {detail}")
        return resp

    def _save(self, resp, stem):
        ext = ".zip" if "zip" in resp.headers.get("content-type", "") else ".swc"
        out = Path(f"{stem}{ext}")
        out.write_bytes(resp.content)
        return out

    def trace_neutube(self, tif, out="output"):
        with open(tif, "rb") as f:
            resp = self._post("/trace_neutube", files={"file": f})
        return self._save(resp, out)

    def app2_subtree(self, tif_path, s1, s2, out="subtree"):
        resp = self._post(
            "/trace_vaa3d_app2_subtree",
            data={"tif_path": tif_path, "s1": s1, "s2": s2},
        )
        return self._save(resp, out)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    client = TraceClient()
    print(client.app2_subtree(
        "/data2/public_data/CWMBS/image/SN21.tif",
        s1="242.8440,249.8640,7.9980",
        s2="243.5728,248.0015,7.9980",
        out="SN21_seed1",
    ))

docs.title: Input Formats
docs.text: This page documents exactly what the service accepts for image volumes and seed points, based on the parsing and preprocessing code in app_helpers.py, vaa3d_utils.py, and subtree_utils.py.

docs.title: Accepted file types
docs.text:
The service validates the file suffix (case-insensitive) against:

.tif  .tiff  .png  .jpg  .jpeg

An unsupported suffix returns 400 Unsupported file type: <suffix>.

3D volumes only

Although image suffixes such as .png/.jpg are accepted by the suffix check, every tracing route requires a 3D array. After reading the image the service asserts img.ndim == 3; otherwise it returns 400 Expected 3D volume, got shape=<shape>. In practice this means a multi-page TIFF stack (Z, Y, X).

docs.title: Two ways to supply a volume
docs.text:
Source Field Used by Multipart upload file all routes Server-side path tif_path subtree routes only
  • file is a standard multipart upload (-F "file=@...").
  • tif_path is an absolute path on the API server. It is expanded with ~ support, validated to exist and be a regular file, then copied into the run's working directory. It is never resolved on the client machine.

The plain tracing routes (/trace_neutube, /trace_vaa3d_app2, /trace_vaa3d_smartTrace) accept only file. The subtree routes accept exactly one of file or tif_path — providing both or neither returns 400 Provide exactly one of file or tif_path.

docs.title: Preprocessing
docs.text:
Every uploaded or referenced volume goes through the same normalization before tracing:

  1. Read with tifffile.imread.
  2. Min-max normalize to uint8 in [0, 255] (to_uint8_0_255). A flat volume (max <= min) becomes all zeros.
  3. Assert the array is 3D.
  4. Write the normalized uint8 stack to vol_uint8.tiff inside the run directory, which is the actual input handed to the tracer.

docs.title: Seed Points
docs.text: Subtree routes require two form fields, s1 and s2, parsed by parse_seed_points. Each describes one or more 3D points in x, y, z order.

docs.title: Single point
docs.text:
A single point may be written with commas, spaces, or wrapped in brackets or parentheses — all of these are equivalent:

242.8440,249.8640,7.9980
242.8440 249.8640 7.9980
[242.8440, 249.8640, 7.9980]
(242.8440 249.8640 7.9980)

Each point must contain exactly three numeric values, otherwise the request fails with 400 s1[...] must contain exactly 3 numbers or 400 s1[...] contains non-numeric values.

docs.title: Multiple points (seed pairs)
docs.text:
To process several seed pairs in one request, send multiple points in both s1 and s2. Points are separated by ; (a | is also accepted as a separator):

s1=10,20,30;40,50,60
s2=11,20,30;42,50,60

This defines two ordered pairs: (10,20,30) -> (11,20,30) and (40,50,60) -> (42,50,60).

docs.title: JSON arrays
docs.text:
s1/s2 may instead be JSON. A single point is a flat array of three numbers; multiple points are a list of triples:

s1=[10,20,30]
s1=[[10,20,30],[40,50,60]]

docs.title: Pairing rules
docs.text:
s1 and s2 are zipped index-by-index into ordered pairs. The following constraints are enforced (normalize_seed_pairs):

Condition Result s1 and s2 have different point counts 400 s1 and s2 must contain the same number of points no points supplied 400 At least one seed pair is required a pair has s1 == s2 (zero distance) 400 s1 and s2 must be different points

docs.title: Output shape by pair count
docs.text:
Seed pairs Response exactly 1 a single subtree.swc 2 or more subtrees.zip containing one SWC per pair

See Algorithms for how each s1 -> s2 pair is turned into a directional subtree.
